name: round 1: one deal, one link
tests: Fill: after createDeal then fill, the maker holds buyAmount more of buyToken, the taker holds sellAmount more of sellToken, and the contract holds nothing of either
All or nothing: a fill by a taker who lacks the tokens or the allowance fails and changes no balance
Private and open: a deal with a taker is filled only by that address; a deal with address(0) is filled by anyone
Once: a deal fills once; a filled or cancelled deal cannot be filled or cancelled again
Expiry: a fill at or after the expiry fails; the maker can still cancel and holds every token again
Cancel: only the maker cancels; then the maker holds every token again and a fill fails
Refused at creation: a zero amount, the same token on both sides, an expiry that is not in the future
Awkward tokens: a token whose transfer returns nothing (as USDT does) works as sellToken and as buyToken
Re-entry: a token that calls back into fill or cancel during its transfer cannot make a deal pay twice
Nobody else: besides createDeal, fill and cancel, no function of the contract changes anything; no constructor argument, no fallback, nothing payable
Interface: ids count up from 1, getDeal returns each deal's terms and status, an unknown id has status None, and createDeal, fill and cancel emit their events
Show: an open deal's link shows what the taker pays and receives, the maker and the expiry, with no wallet in the browser
Fill from the page: with a wallet that holds the tokens, at most four presses of primary-action end with the deal filled on the chain and deal-status saying so
States: a filled, a cancelled and an expired deal, and an id that does not exist, each say so and offer no fill
Not for you: a deal reserved for one address, opened with another wallet, names the address it is for and offers no fill
Create from the page: the form at /#/new and at most four presses of primary-action end with a link in deal-link to a deal with exactly the entered terms, which its taker can fill
